ace_builtin_node_reference.overview: Reference for commonly used ACE built-in nodes. For the complete, authoritative list see: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/app-connect/13.0.x?topic=development-built-in-nodes Always verify xmi:type namespace prefixes using the ace-bob skill before use.

category.name: Input_Nodes
category.description: Nodes that receive messages and start a message flow.

node.name: HTTP Input
node.purpose: Receives HTTP/HTTPS requests (REST or SOAP over HTTP)

key_properties.property: URL pattern to match, e.g. /MyService/* or /*
Message domain for parsing (XMLNSC, JSON, BLOB etc.)
Seconds to wait for flow to complete before timing out the client

node.usage_notes: The catch terminal fires when an unhandled exception occurs in the flow. Always connect the catch terminal to an error handler subflow.

node.name: HTTP Reply
node.purpose: Sends the HTTP response back to the caller
node.usage_notes: Must be connected for every synchronous HTTP flow. Set OutputRoot.HTTPResponseHeader."X-Original-HTTP-Status-Code" before this node to control the HTTP response code.

node.name: MQ Input
node.purpose: Reads messages from an IBM MQ queue

key_properties.property: Name of the MQ queue to read from (REQUIRED)

node.name: MQ Output
node.purpose: Writes messages to an IBM MQ queue

node.name: File Input
node.purpose: Reads files from a directory
node.usage_notes: InputLocalEnvironment.File.Name contains the filename. InputLocalEnvironment.File.Directory contains the directory path.

node.name: Email Output
node.purpose: Sends email messages

key_properties.property: SMTP server hostname (can be configured as UDP)

node.usage_notes: Set OutputRoot.EmailOutputHeader.To, .From, .Subject before this node. Message body must be set as BLOB in OutputRoot.BLOB.BLOB.

category.name: Processing_Nodes
category.description: Nodes that transform, route, or process messages.

node.name: Compute
node.purpose: Executes ESQL to transform, route, or manipulate messages

key_properties.property: JDBC data source name for database access (only if DB queries needed)

node.usage_notes: The ESQL module must be a CREATE COMPUTE MODULE with a Main function returning BOOLEAN. Return TRUE to propagate to 'out', FALSE to suppress propagation. Use PROPAGATE TO TERMINAL 'out1' etc. for multiple output terminals.

node.name: Filter
node.purpose: Routes messages based on a boolean ESQL expression
node.usage_notes: Use CREATE FILTER MODULE (not COMPUTE MODULE). The Main function must RETURN TRUE or FALSE. The 'unknown' terminal fires when the expression cannot be evaluated.

node.name: Flow Order
node.purpose: Propagates message to multiple output terminals in sequence
node.usage_notes: Used to trigger multiple downstream paths in a defined order. Commonly used to sequence audit logging before and after main processing.

node.name: HTTP Request
node.purpose: Makes an outbound HTTP/HTTPS request to a backend service

key_properties.property: Seconds to wait for backend response

node.usage_notes: Set OutputLocalEnvironment.Destination.HTTP.RequestURL dynamically in the preceding Compute node to route to different backends. Set OutputLocalEnvironment.Destination.HTTP.RequestLine.Method for PUT/POST/GET/DELETE. The 'error' terminal fires when the backend returns an HTTP error status.

node.name: TryCatch
node.purpose: Catches exceptions thrown within its contained sub-flow
node.terminals: try (wraps the happy path), catch (fires on exception)
node.usage_notes: Wrap sections of a flow that might throw exceptions. The catch terminal receives the original message plus InputExceptionList. Use THROW USER EXCEPTION in ESQL to signal anticipated errors.

node.name: Route
node.purpose: Routes messages to different terminals based on message content
node.usage_notes: Alternative to chained Filter nodes when routing to many paths. Configure routing conditions in the node properties.

node.name: Database
node.purpose: Executes a database operation using an SQL statement
node.usage_notes: For complex queries or inserts, prefer using a Compute node with dataSource set and ESQL SELECT/PASSTHRU statements for full flexibility.

node.name: Trace
node.purpose: Writes message content to a trace file for debugging

key_properties.property: Absolute file path for trace output
ESQL expression defining what to trace

node.usage_notes: Use for development/debugging only. Remove or disable in production flows to avoid performance impact and disk space consumption.

node.name: Timeout_Control
node.purpose: Schedules or controls timeout events for timer-based flows
node.usage_notes: Used with TimeoutNotification node to implement scheduled/recurring processing. Set OutputLocalEnvironment.TimeoutRequest.StartTime, OutputLocalEnvironment.TimeoutRequest.Interval (seconds), and OutputLocalEnvironment.TimeoutRequest.Count (-1 for forever).

node.name: Timeout_Notification
node.purpose: Fires a message at a scheduled time or interval
node.usage_notes: Starting node for timer-driven flows (scheduled batch jobs, polling).

node.name: XSL_Transform
node.purpose: Applies an XSLT stylesheet to transform XML messages

key_properties.property: Path to the XSLT file relative to the project

node.name: Java_Compute
node.purpose: Executes Java code to process messages
node.usage_notes: The Java class must extend MbJavaComputeNode and implement evaluate(). Use when ESQL cannot achieve the required transformation (e.g., complex string manipulation, file I/O, calling external Java libraries).

node.name: Validate
node.purpose: Validates the message against a schema (XSD, WSDL)

node.name: Mapping
node.purpose: Graphical message mapping using a .map file
node.usage_notes: Preferred for structural message transformations where a visual map is easier to maintain than ESQL.

category.name: Subflow_Terminals
category.description: Special nodes used in subflow files.

node.name: Subflow Input
node.purpose: Entry point terminal of a subflow

node.name: Subflow Output
node.purpose: Exit point terminal of a subflow

node_connection_rules.rule: Every input node's catch/failure terminal MUST be connected to an error handler.
Every HTTP Input node needs a corresponding HTTP Reply node on the successful path.
HTTP Request node 'error' terminal should connect to an error handler that re-throws or wraps the upstream error.
TryCatch 'catch' terminal receives InputExceptionList — always extract error details from it in the downstream Compute node.
FlowOrder terminals (first, second) fire in sequence — use this for audit/logging patterns where you want guaranteed ordering.
